tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y): The starting coordinates for `left_click_drag`.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user. Call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and it boots one that is off and returns while that one is still starting up. Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches: the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition: 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'set_posture' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'state': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'posture' reports the state, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the state and angle with 'posture'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'set_posture' and take a 'screenshot'; if the open screen shows the app with black bars and the target sets UIRequiresFullScreen, tell the user the key is the likely cause and keep it unless they ask; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag: left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator this session already uses, else a booted one no other session is using, else the first booted one. If none is booted, 'attach' boots the only one the user already allowed, and 'launch' does so or asks for 'attach' first; if there is not exactly one, name one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

angle.description: For 'set_posture' with state 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. # Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

## Writing the test

- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.

## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage

- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.

self.plan()
        subscription.retrieve.return_value = chargebee_says('active')
        self.assertEqual(self.delete().status_code, 204)
        subscription.cancel_for_items.assert_called_once_with('sub_1', {'end_of_term': False}, env=mock.ANY)
        self.assertTrue(self.gone())
        self.assertFalse(JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user_id=self.user.id).exists())

    def test_a_plan_chargebee_already_cancelled_is_not_cancelled_again(self, subscription):
        self.plan()
        subscription.retrieve.return_value = chargebee_says('cancelled')
        self.assertEqual(self.delete().status_code, 204)
        subscription.cancel_for_items.assert_not_called()
        self.assertTrue(self.gone())

    def test_a_plan_chargebee_no_longer_has_is_not_cancelled(self, subscription):
        self.plan()
        subscription.retrieve.side_effect = chargebee.InvalidRequestError(
            404, {'message': "Sorry, we couldn't find that resource", 'type': 'invalid_request',
             'api_error_code': 'resource_not_found', 'error_code': 'resource_not_found'})
        self.assertEqual(self.delete().status_code, 204)
        subscription.cancel_for_items.assert_not_called()

class PrintReportTestCase(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=1, defaults={'name': 'base'})
        self.user = User.objects.create(email=f'report-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com')
        ensure_lots(self.user.id)
        application = Application.objects.create(client_id='JusPrin2', name='JusPrin 2', client_type='public',
                                                 authorization_grant_type='authorization-code')
        token = AccessToken.objects.create(user=self.user, application=application, token=uuid.uuid4().hex,
                                           expires=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1), scope='read write')
        self.client = Client(HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {token.token}')
        storage = mock.patch('jusprin.v2.views.save_file_obj', side_effect=lambda path, *a, **k: (path, f'https://store/{path}'))
        self.stored = storage.start()
        self.addCleanup(storage.stop)

    def report(self, gcode_hash='a71f8c04', text=TEXT, outcome='partly', photos=None, facts=None):
        return self.client.post(URL, {
            'gcode_hash': gcode_hash, 'outcome': outcome, 'text': text,
            'facts': json.dumps(facts if facts is not None else {'project': 'Vent Grille', 'printer': 'Bambu X1C'}),
            'photos': [jpeg()] if photos is None else photos,
        })

    def rewards(self):
        return CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=self.user, kind=CreditGrant.REWARD)

    def total(self):
        return account(self.user)['credits']['total']


class SubmitTests(PrintReportTestCase):
    def test_a_good_report_earns_25_credits_at_once_that_never_expire(self):
        before = self.total()
        response = self.report()
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 201)
        self.assertEqual(response.json()['credits'], 25)
        report = PrintReport.objects.get(user=self.user)
        self.assertEqual(report.outcome, 'partly')
        self.assertEqual(report.facts['printer'], 'Bambu X1C')
        self.assertEqual(len(report.photos), 1)
        self.assertTrue(self.stored.called)
        lot = self.rewards().get()
        self.assertEqual(lot.source_ref, f'report:{report.id}')
        self.assertIsNone(lot.expires_at)
        self.assertEqual(self.total(), before + 25)

    def test_it_shows_in_the_activity(self):
        self.report()

class WebhookTests(BillingTestCase):
    URL = '/ent/jusprin/v2/cb_webhook'

    def post(self, posted, kept, current=None):
        """Posts an event to the webhook, with JusPrin 2's site keeping the event
        `kept` under that id (None: it has no such event) and the subscription
        `current` as it is now."""
        with mock.patch('chargebee.Subscription.retrieve',
                        return_value=SimpleNamespace(subscription=SimpleNamespace(values=current))):
            return self._post(posted, kept)

    def _post(self, posted, kept):
        if kept is None:
            retrieve = mock.patch('chargebee.Event.retrieve', side_effect=chargebee.InvalidRequestError(
                404, {'message': 'not found', 'type': 'invalid_request', 'api_error_code': 'resource_not_found',
                      'error_code': 'resource_not_found'}))
        else:
            retrieve = mock.patch('chargebee.Event.retrieve',
                                  return_value=SimpleNamespace(event=SimpleNamespace(values=kept)))
        with retrieve as retrieved:
            response = Client().post(self.URL, json.dumps(posted), content_type='application/json')
        return response, retrieved

    def test_a_plans_event_is_read_back_from_jusprins_site(self):
        renewed = event('subscription_renewed', subscription=sub(self.user))
        response, retrieved = self.post({'id': 'ev-1'}, renewed, sub(self.user))
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, self.lots()), (200, [('subscription', 750)]))
        self.assertEqual(retrieved.call_args.args, ('ev-1',))
        self.assertEqual(retrieved.call_args.kwargs['env'].site, 'jusprinv2-test')

    def test_a_term_is_granted_when_its_invoice_is_paid(self):

                'subscription_id': 'sub-1', 'line_items': []}
        self.post({'id': 'ev-2'}, event('payment_succeeded', invoice=paid, subscription=sub(self.user)), sub(self.user))
        self.assertEqual(self.lots(), [('subscription', 750)])

    def test_a_late_event_does_not_undo_a_later_switch(self):

# Printers and filament

How to choose the printer and filament a project prints with, and how to add and manage your printers.

Names in bold are the words on screen. On a Mac the menus named here are in the menu bar. On Windows and Linux the **File** menu is the **File** button in the title bar, and the other menus are in the menu beside it.

These are the by-hand steps. I can change printer and filament settings myself with my settings tools; adding and connecting a printer happens in the printer's own chat, which these steps open.

## The printer and filament in a project

The header of an open project shows the project's printer and its filament side by side, for example "Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4" and "PLA". With none chosen they read **Select printer** and **Select filament**. Click either one to open its menu.

The printer's menu has:

- The printer's name and how it is connected, such as **Ready**, **Printing**, **Offline** or **Not connected**. Click it to open the printer's own window.
- **Nozzle**, the nozzle size the project is set up for. It cannot be changed here.
- **Plate**: click it to choose the plate type that is on the printer, such as a textured or a smooth plate.
- **OTHER PRINTERS**: click one to slice the project for that printer instead.
- **Printer settings…**, **Ask AI about printer settings…**, **Calibrate…** and **Add a printer…**.

When a project file brought its own printer, the printer is marked **From the file · not one of your printers**.

## Choose the filament and its colour

Click the filament in the header. The menu has:

- **COLOUR**: click a colour to set the filament's colour. The + after them (**Other colour…**) opens a colour picker.
- **FILAMENTS FOR THIS PRINTER**: click one to print with it, or **Other filament…** to pick from all of them.
- **Use what's loaded on the printer…**, when the printer reports what is loaded in it.
- **Filament settings…**, **Ask AI about filament settings…** and **Calibrate this filament…**.

To print in two or more filaments, click **Add another filament to this print**. The menu then lists each filament by its number; click one to choose its filament and colour. To say which filament an object prints in, use **Change filament** in its menu in the Plates tab.

## The Printer menu

The **Printer** menu has the same commands for the open project: **Add a printer…**, **Printer settings…**, **Ask AI about printer settings…**, **Filament settings…**, **Ask AI about filament settings…** and **Calibrate…**. It works from Home too.

With no printer chosen yet, **Printer settings…** starts adding a printer instead, and **Calibrate…** is greyed out.

## Add a printer

1. On Home, click **+ Add printer** at the top of the printers, or choose **Add a printer…** in the **Printer** menu. A chat titled **Add a printer** opens.
2. Say which printer you have, in your own words, or pick it from a list: **Browse the full printer list** at the top of the chat opens a form that asks **Which printer?** and then **Which plate is on it?**.
3. The printer is saved under its own name and shows on Home. You can add two printers of the same model; each gets a name of its own.

If you skipped choosing a printer the first time JusPrin started, it uses a stand-in, a generic 250 mm Klipper printer, until you add yours.

## Connect a printer

Connecting a printer lets JusPrin send prints to it and show how it is doing. JusPrin connects Bambu Lab printers, and printers it reaches at an address on your network, such as Klipper printers through Moonraker, OctoPrint, PrusaLink and Elegoo Link.

1. On Home, click **Connect…** on the printer's card, or open the card's menu (**Printer actions**) and choose **Connect…**.
2. The printer's chat asks for what it needs, such as its address. A Bambu Lab printer also needs its **Access code**, and a print host may need its **API key**. These stay on this computer.
3. **Help me find the code** explains where to find it on the printer.

A Bambu Lab printer needs Bambu's network plug-in. The chat says so when it is missing.

## Rename or remove a printer

Open the printer card's menu on Home (**Printer actions**):

- **Rename**, then type the new name under **Printer name** and click **Save**. A name cannot be empty, hold any of < > [ ] : / \ | ? * ", or be the name of another printer.
- **Remove printer…**, then **Remove**. The printer's own settings are deleted; your projects stay.
- **Printer settings…** and **Ask AI about printer settings…** open its settings.

## Bring printers from another slicer

In the **Printer** menu choose **Import printers from JusPrin 1…**, or the item above it, which imports from the slicer JusPrin is built on. The printers come with their filaments and print settings, and the other program keeps its own copy. JusPrin offers the same the first time it starts, when it finds them on the computer.

## Calibrate a printer or a filament

Calibration prints a small test, such as a temperature tower, and then sets the printer or filament from what the test shows.

1. Choose **Calibrate…** in the printer's menu, the **Printer** menu or the printer card's menu on Home, or **Calibrate this filament…** in the filament's menu.
2. A question names the printer and filament. Click **Start**. The open project is saved and closed, and the test opens as a project of its own, with a chat that asks which test to print.

Calibration needs AI. When it is not set up, the question offers **Set up AI…** instead of Start.

# Misrouted failures: final report (2026-11-25)

All 42 cases from `error-handling-misrouted-failures.md` now have an end state: fixed with a
test, shown not to happen, or waiting on Kenneth. Nothing is committed or pushed in either
repository. The JusPrin work is in the worktree
`/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/misrouted-failures` (branch
`claude/misrouted-failures`). The server work is uncommitted in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`.
Each case's evidence is in `misrouted-failures-handover.md`; the proposed sentences are in
`misrouted-failures-sentences.md`.

## Tests at the end
- agent_bridge_tests, jusprin_tests, jusprin_update_tests, jusprin_profile_tests: all pass.
- AgentUI vitest 846 tests, HomeUI vitest 169 tests: pass.
- Shell harness, every mode: see the sweep result in the session's last message.
- Server: `jusprin` and `app_ent` suites, 404 tests OK.

## Decision needed

**The sign-in that fails at our token endpoint (case 11).** When our server's token endpoint
fails (a 500, an error answer, or nothing listening) the app shows "Signing in didn't finish… Try
again." and we never hear of it. Pressing Cancel on the consent page reaches the app in exactly
the same way, because OrcaSlicer's sign-in job hands JusPrin only a translated message ("Unknown
error"). It is your call because the only way to tell the two apart is a small additive field in
OrcaSlicer's OAuthJob saying which step failed, which is a line in an OrcaSlicer-owned file that
every rebase carries. Option one: add the field, so our failures are reported and Cancel stays
quiet; it costs one small seam. Option two: leave it, and our token endpoint's failures stay
invisible unless the server's own Sentry catches them (it does for a 500, not for nothing
listening). I'd add the field. Should I add it?

**The print report that could not be sent (case 6).** When the app gets no answer at all while
sending a print report, it says "The report couldn't be sent. Check your connection and try
again." Every answer our server gives is already read or reported. This has the same shape as the
case you dropped earlier with "This error msg is reasonable", so I read your answer as covering
it and changed nothing. Option one: agree, and nothing changes. Option two: you want it handled
differently, which needs your wording. My pick is option one. Does your earlier answer cover this
one too?

**A project that a crash left mid-restore disappears from Home for good (case 15).** If the app
crashes while a chat is being restored into a project, it leaves a marker file in that project.
From then on the project's card is gone from Home, opening it fails, and nothing ever removes the
marker; we only get a log line. It is your call because the fix changes what the person sees on
Home. Option one: on start, finish or undo the interrupted restore and remove the marker, and
report it to us once; the project comes back. Option two: keep the project hidden but report it,
so at least we hear of it. I'd take option one. Should I build the recovery?

**The jusprin-mcp helper cannot report a failure of ours (case 20).** When an outside AI client
(such as Claude Desktop) talks to JusPrin through the jusprin-mcp helper, and JusPrin answers the
helper wrongly or not at all, the client is now told "JusPrin is open, but it did not answer the
bridge… This is a fault in JusPrin" and the reason goes to the client's log. It still never
reaches us, because the helper has no Sentry. It is your call because adding Sentry to a helper
that runs inside someone else's AI client sends data from a new place. Option one: add the same
crash and error reporting the app has, behind the same automatic-reports setting; it costs a
Sentry setup in the helper's build. Option two: leave it log-only. I'd take option one. Should the
helper report to us?

**A kept G-code file that changed on disk (part of case 21).** Print history keeps a copy of each
G-code it sent. If that copy changes on disk, the entry says "Kept file changed on disk · slice
again to print it", which is a next step that works, but only the app writes that store, so the
cause is ours and we never hear of it. Reporting from the Print history page itself would fire on
every redraw. Option one: report it once when the change is first noticed; it needs a small
"already reported" record. Option two: leave it, since the person can carry on. I'd take option
one. Should I report it once?

**The new sentences.** Six sentences of ours are proposed in `misrouted-failures-sentences.md`,
each with where it shows and what it replaces: the chat too long for the model (case 35, already
with you), a project open in another JusPrin window (14), a dropped file the page cannot read
(21), OrcaSlicer's settings file JusPrin cannot read during import (21), a Moonraker printer that
needs an API key (36), and a plan whose renewal payment was declined (38). None is built. Which of
them do you approve as written?

## Changed behavior worth knowing before review
- Deleting an account whose Chargebee subscription Chargebee cannot find now stops with
  "Something went wrong on our side" and reports to us. Before, it deleted the account. The
  answer cannot tell a subscription deleted in Chargebee from one on a site this server no longer
  reads, which would go on billing the person.
- On Credits and plans, a checkout or a return from paying that arrives without the browser's
  sign-in now shows "Something went wrong on our side" and reports. Before, it silently went back
  to the prices page, which showed "Sign up to buy" to someone who had just paid.
- JusPrin 1's checkout no longer drops the Obico Pro discount when Chargebee cannot confirm the
  Obico subscription; the checkout stops instead.

## Follow-ups found on the way, not fixed
- Anthropic refused one of our requests because a web_search tool use in the chat history had no
  matching result block (Sentry issue OBICO-SERVER-B2N, 2 events on 2026-11-22). That is a bug
  of ours in how history is replayed.
- JusPrin 1's checkout callback raises a 500 if Chargebee ever sends a cancelled checkout to it.
  The checkout sets no cancel URL, and Sentry has no such event in 90 days, so it was not
  reproduced or changed.

`/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/misrouted-failures` (branch
`claude/misrouted-failures`). The server work is uncommitted in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`.
Each case's evidence is in `misrouted-failures-handover.md`; the proposed sentences are in
`misrouted-failures-sentences.md`.

## Tests at the end
- agent_bridge_tests, jusprin_tests, jusprin_update_tests, jusprin_profile_tests: all pass.
- AgentUI vitest 846 tests, HomeUI vitest 169 tests: pass.
- Shell harness, every mode: see the sweep result in the session's last message.
- Server: `jusprin` and `app_ent` suites, 404 tests OK.

## Decision needed

**The sign-in that fails at our token endpoint (case 11).** When our server's token endpoint
fails (a 500, an error answer, or nothing listening) the app shows "Signing in didn't finish… Try
again." and we never hear of it. Pressing Cancel on the consent page reaches the app in exactly
the same way, because OrcaSlicer's sign-in job hands JusPrin only a translated message ("Unknown
error"). It is your call because the only way to tell the two apart is a small additive field in
OrcaSlicer's OAuthJob saying which step failed, which is a line in an OrcaSlicer-owned file that
every rebase carries. Option one: add the field, so our failures are reported and Cancel stays
quiet; it costs one small seam. Option two: leave it, and our token endpoint's failures stay
invisible unless the server's own Sentry catches them (it does for a 500, not for nothing
listening). I'd add the field. Should I add it?

**The print report that could not be sent (case 6).** When the app gets no answer at all while
sending a print report, it says "The report couldn't be sent. Check your connection and try
again." Every answer our server gives is already read or reported. This has the same shape as the
case you dropped earlier with "This error msg is reasonable", so I read your answer as covering
it and changed nothing. Option one: agree, and nothing changes. Option two: you want it handled
differently, which needs your wording. My pick is option one. Does your earlier answer cover this
one too?

**A project that a crash left mid-restore disappears from Home for good (case 15).** If the app
crashes while a chat is being restored into a project, it leaves a marker file in that project.
From then on the project's card is gone from Home, opening it fails, and nothing ever removes the
marker; we only get a log line. It is your call because the fix changes what the person sees on
Home. Option one: on start, finish or undo the interrupted restore and remove the marker, and
report it to us once; the project comes back. Option two: keep the project hidden but report it,
so at least we hear of it. I'd take option one. Should I build the recovery?

**The jusprin-mcp helper cannot report a failure of ours (case 20).** When an outside AI client
(such as Claude Desktop) talks to JusPrin through the jusprin-mcp helper, and JusPrin answers the
helper wrongly or not at all, the client is now told "JusPrin is open, but it did not answer the
bridge… This is a fault in JusPrin" and the reason goes to the client's log. It still never
reaches us, because the helper has no Sentry. It is your call because adding Sentry to a helper
that runs inside someone else's AI client sends data from a new place. Option one: add the same
crash and error reporting the app has, behind the same automatic-reports setting; it costs a
Sentry setup in the helper's build. Option two: leave it log-only. I'd take option one. Should the
helper report to us?

**A kept G-code file that changed on disk (part of case 21).** Print history keeps a copy of each
G-code it sent. If that copy changes on disk, the entry says "Kept file changed on disk · slice
again to print it", which is a next step that works, but only the app writes that store, so the
cause is ours and we never hear of it. Reporting from the Print history page itself would fire on
every redraw. Option one: report it once when the change is first noticed; it needs a small
"already reported" record. Option two: leave it, since the person can carry on. I'd take option
one. Should I report it once?

**The new sentences.** Six sentences of ours are proposed in `misrouted-failures-sentences.md`,
each with where it shows and what it replaces: the chat too long for the model (case 35, already
with you), a project open in another JusPrin window (14), a dropped file the page cannot read
(21), OrcaSlicer's settings file JusPrin cannot read during import (21), a Moonraker printer that
needs an API key (36), and a plan whose renewal payment was declined (38). None is built. Which of
them do you approve as written?

## Changed behavior worth knowing before review
- Deleting an account whose Chargebee subscription Chargebee cannot find now stops with
  "Something went wrong on our side" and reports to us. Before, it deleted the account. The
  answer cannot tell a subscription deleted in Chargebee from one on a site this server no longer
  reads, which would go on billing the person.
- On Credits and plans, a checkout or a return from paying that arrives without the browser's
  sign-in now shows "Something went wrong on our side" and reports. Before, it silently went back
  to the prices page, which showed "Sign up to buy" to someone who had just paid.
- JusPrin 1's checkout no longer drops the Obico Pro discount when Chargebee cannot confirm the
  Obico subscription; the checkout stops instead.

## Follow-ups found on the way, not fixed
- Anthropic refused one of our requests because a web_search tool use in the chat history had no
  matching result block (Sentry issue OBICO-SERVER-B2N, 2 events on 2026-11-22). That is a bug
  of ours in how history is replayed.
- JusPrin 1's checkout callback raises a 500 if Chargebee ever sends a cancelled checkout to it.
  The checkout sets no cancel URL, and Sentry has no such event in 90 days, so it was not
  reproduced or changed.

content.text:
Every one of the 42 cases now ends in one of the three states: fixed with a test that failed first, shown not to happen, or waiting on a decision of Kenneth's. Nothing is committed or pushed in either repository. Five questions and the new sentences are in [misrouted-failures-final-report.md](</Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_cd3120f7-030a-4af8-a6d1-28ecae789f1a/misrouted-failures-final-report.md>), written as "Decision needed" paragraphs. The evidence for each case is in `misrouted-failures-handover.md` in the same folder.

**Fixed in this last stretch:**
- **AI exports to a folder the system won't let the app write (case 32).** All four export kinds now say the system's words, for example "A preset file could not be written. macOS says: “Permission denied”." They are no longer reported to us. For presets, OrcaSlicer's writer throws the reason away, so the app writes a small probe file beside the preset with the same writer, reads the reason from that, and deletes the probe.
- **A failed Save preset.** Its message named OrcaSlicer, which the model must never read. It now says "The app could not write the preset … macOS says: “…”", and a harness check covers it.
- **Billing guesses (case 24):**
  - The billing page no longer reads any Chargebee failure as "no card on file". One existing test had been calling the real Chargebee API and passed only because of that guess; it now uses a stub.
  - Deleting an account whose subscription Chargebee can't find now stops and reports to us. Before, the account was deleted. Chargebee's answer can't tell a deleted subscription from one on a site this server no longer reads, and that one would keep billing the person.
  - A print-report database conflict is only called "already reported" when a report really exists.
- **Checkout (case 25).** A checkout, or a return from paying, that arrives without the sign-in now shows "Something went wrong on our side" and reports to us. Before, it went back to the prices page, which showed "Sign up to buy" to someone who had just paid.
- **Unknown Chargebee event IDs (case 23).** A webhook post whose event ID JusPrin's Chargebee site doesn't hold still gets a 400, but is now logged.
- **JusPrin 1 payment code (case 27):**
  - A paid subscription that matches no account now raises an error. Before, it answered OK and logged nothing.
  - Checkout no longer drops the Obico Pro discount when Chargebee can't confirm the Obico subscription; it stops instead.
  - The plan list no longer swallows its errors.

**Shown not to happen:**
- **Case 26:** a deactivated account, or a token from the wrong app or scope. Only an admin can deactivate an account, and sign-in then tells the person their account is inactive. The app only ever asks for its own client with "read write".
- **Case 27, the cancelled checkout:** JusPrin 1's checkout callback would raise a 500 on a cancelled checkout. Sentry has no such event in 90 days, and whether Chargebee ever sends cancels there depends on Obico's Chargebee settings, which only production credentials show. I left it unchanged.

**Tests run:**
- agent_bridge_tests, jusprin_tests, jusprin_update_tests and jusprin_profile_tests all pass.
- AgentUI vitest: 846 tests pass. HomeUI vitest: 169 tests pass.
- All eight shell-harness modes pass, and the default mode passes again after the final changes.
- clang-tidy passes on the changed lines. jusprin-mcp builds.
- Server: 404 tests pass across `jusprin` and `app_ent`.

**Waiting on Kenneth:**
- Five decisions:
  - an additive OrcaSlicer field to tell a failure at our token endpoint from Cancel (case 11);
  - whether his earlier "reasonable" answer covers the print-report message (case 6);
  - recovering a project left hidden by a crash during a chat restore (case 15);
  - letting the jusprin-mcp helper report to us (case 20);
  - reporting a changed kept G-code file once (case 21).
- Six new sentences, for cases 35, 14, 21 (two), 36 and 38.

**Cleanup:**
- Done: the scratch apps, their data folders, the stand-in processes and their orphaned crash handlers are gone.
- Left for you: a safety check refused deleting 14 harness data folders under `$TMPDIR`. The report lists them by name; please delete them yourself.

content.content:
1	# What to do with the two reviews (2026-11-25)
2	
3	Two independent reviewers read your uncommitted change against the Error handling rules. They were
4	given the code and the rules, not your notes' conclusions. Their reports are beside this file:
5	`misrouted-failures-review-app.md` (18 findings) and `misrouted-failures-review-server.md` (13).
6	Read both in full first. The change is not ready to land. This file says how to treat the findings
7	and answers the questions in your final report. It comes from the session that started you, not
8	from Kenneth, except where his words are quoted.
9	
10	## How to work through them
11	- Each finding is a claim. Show it first (a failing test, or the real app), then fix it, then show
12	  it fixed. If a finding does not hold, say why with evidence and leave the code.
13	- Order: app findings 1, 2, 3 and server finding 1 first. They are a path to lost work, an app that
14	  may end on a menu click, and replies that can be had for free.
15	- Do not end your turn to wait, and do not end it per group. End it when every finding has an end
16	  state.
17	- Commit nothing, push nothing.
18	
19	## The pattern behind most findings
20	Most of them are one of two mistakes, and both are the ones the rules warn about.
21	
22	1. Deciding by the kind of error and not by its cause. `refused_by_system` looks at an exception
23	   type and four errno values, and the catch at the top of every page message applies it to
24	   whatever comes up. The rules say: "A status code, an exception type, or the way the failure
25	   arrives … is not a cause." Decide at the operation that knows what it was doing. Where the app
26	   is writing the person's own work to the person's own storage (their projects folder, a folder
27	   they picked for an export, a file they chose), a refusal by the system is the person's, whatever
28	   number the system gave it: a quota, a drive that was unplugged, a file too large for the disk's
29	   format are theirs just as a full disk is. Where the app is reading or writing something only the
30	   app controls (the printer facts file, its own records), a refusal cannot be told from a wrong
31	   path of ours, so it comes to us. Take the system's reason from the call that failed, never from
32	   whatever errno happens to hold afterwards. And a person can only act on "Permission denied" if
33	   they know where: show the folder with it.
34	2. Swinging to "ours". A browser tab left open until its sign-in ended, a file name typed without
35	   ".3mf", a Windows computer where the person declined to install WebView2, GitHub limiting an
36	   office's shared address: each is something only the person can change, or something nobody here
37	   can change. Each now says "Something went wrong on our side" and files a report. Ask of every
38	   branch you changed to "ours": can a person get here by doing something ordinary?
39	
40	## App findings: what is already settled
41	- 1 and 2 (autosave). Stopping autosave for the rest of the run is wrong, because it leaves the
42	  person's work unsaved while the header can say "Saved". A background save's next attempt is new
43	  work, not a retry of the failed one. So: keep trying; report a failure of ours once per project
44	  per run; and never show "Saved" while changes are unsaved. Make the failure of ours reach the
45	  report on every path, including a worker that fails within two seconds.
46	- 3. Every place the new throws can reach needs the reporting handler above it. Walk up from each
47	  new throw to an entry point on every path (menus, keyboard shortcuts, Open Recent, startup).
48	  Show the escape in the real app before fixing it.
49	- 4. A name the person typed is never ours. Accept ".3MF" in any case and add the extension when it
50	  is missing, as a save dialog does.
51	- 5. When a save the system refused blocks New project or a printer switch, the person must be told
52	  why, where they pressed.
53	- 8. Report a panel that cannot start once, not again after 20 seconds and not on every Retry. Do
54	  not call a missing WebView2 ours; find out whether the code can tell that the runtime is missing
55	  (the backend not being available). That one needs a sentence and a run on Windows, so put it on
56	  the waiting list with what you found; do not build a sentence.
57	- 9. Find the server's real answers for too many code requests and confirmations, the same safe way
58	  you did for login (no email sent anywhere), and route them by what they are.
59	- 10. A 404 is the person's only when the service's words say something this person can act on
60	  (their key has no access to the model). "Invalid URL" is ours. Put back a test for the model
61	  that is not found. A service that is down and answers with a web page and no words is still the
62	  service's trouble: not reported, shown with the existing "could not reach the … service" sentence,
63	  because the person does the same thing in both cases.
64	- 11. This corrects what I told you earlier. A rate limit from GitHub leaves the person doing the
65	  same thing as no network (try later), so it shares "Couldn't reach GitHub" and is not reported.

  state.

   whatever comes up. The rules say: "A status code, an exception type, or the way the failure
   arrives … is not a cause." Decide at the operation that knows what it was doing. Where the app
   is writing the person's own work to the person's own storage (their projects folder, a folder
   they picked for an export, a file they chose), a refusal by the system is the person's, whatever
   number the system gave it: a quota, a drive that was unplugged, a file too large for the disk's
   format are theirs just as a full disk is. Where the app is reading or writing something only the
   app controls (the printer facts file, its own records), a refusal cannot be told from a wrong
   path of ours, so it comes to us. Take the system's reason from the call that failed, never from
   whatever errno happens to hold afterwards. And a person can only act on "Permission denied" if
   they know where: show the folder with it.

1	I read the change against the rule and found one money hole, several failures sent to the wrong owner, and two weak tests. Both test suites pass. Everything below is traced in code unless marked; I ran no new tests.
2	
3	All paths are under `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise/web_ent/`.
4	
5	## Findings, most serious first
6	
7	**1. A direct caller can get a delivered reply refunded.** `jusprin/v2/credits.py:70-80`, `jusprin/v2/gateway.py:148-149, 202`.
8	- **Scenario:** Someone calls the gateway with their own script, reads the whole reply, and drops the connection before the last event. The turn stays charged, but no "completed" mark is set. They then send the same turn id with `X-JusPrin-Chat-Title: %FF`, which raises `UnicodeDecodeError` after admission and costs no provider call. The top handler gives the turn's charge back.
9	- **Slower variant:** the "completed" mark lasts one hour (`TURN_TTL_SECONDS`), so replaying a turn id later with a failing request has the same effect.
10	- **Why:** the refund is keyed by turn id, not by whether the failing request made the charge. `admit` knows whether it charged in this call; refunding only then would close it.
11	- **Confidence:** high on the logic, not run.
12	
13	**2. The app's own 120-second limit is treated as "the person stopped".** `jusprin/v2/gateway.py:239-243`.
14	- **Scenario:** The provider stalls or the reply runs long. The app cuts the request at 120 seconds (`ProviderProfile.hpp:64`, set as `CURLOPT_TIMEOUT`), while the server waits up to 300. The server sees a disconnect, keeps the charge and reports nothing. The person retries under a new turn id and pays again.
15	- **Why:** a failure on our side is recorded as the person's choice.
16	- **Confidence:** high on the code path; unconfirmed how often replies pass 120 seconds.
17	
18	**3. Billing and usage now fails for a paid account with no customer on JusPrin 2's Chargebee site.** `jusprin/ledger/billing.py:152-156`, `jusprin/ledger/ledger.py:35-44`.
19	- **Scenario:** `has_paid` is true for a JusPrin 1 plan row, a plan row made in the admin, or a plan bought before the 2026-11-10 move to JusPrin's own site. Chargebee answers "not found" for these, every time, so the page is a 500 for that person on every visit.
20	- **Why:** the new docstring says such an account always has a customer; `ensure_customer` in the same file treats a missing customer as normal.
21	- **Gap in the test:** the new test covers only a 401.
22	- **Confidence:** high in code; unconfirmed whether production has such accounts.
23	
24	**4. Starting a checkout without a signed-in browser is sent to us, but it is a stale page.** `jusprin/v2/web.py:305-306`.
25	- **How it is reached:** the post needs a valid CSRF cookie and token, so strangers and crawlers get Django's 403 and never reach it. What does reach it is a tab left open past the 60-day session, a guest link (`?guest=1` logs out without changing the CSRF cookie) opened later in the same browser, or an account deleted while the page is open.
26	- **Why:** all of these are the person's, and the report names no account, so we cannot act on it. `billing_page`, `cancel` and `portal` in the same file treat the same cause as the person's.
27	- **Confidence:** high.
28	
29	**5. Opening the checkout return address without an id files a report.** `jusprin/v2/web.py:325-326`.
30	- **Scenario:** the address is a public GET with no sign-in check before the raise. Any scanner or person who requests it gets a 500 and files "Chargebee sent the person back…", though nothing ties the request to Chargebee.
31	- **Confidence:** high on reachability; volume unconfirmed.
32	
33	**6. Coming back from paying without the session shows "Something went wrong on our side" to someone whose payment succeeded.** `jusprin/v2/web.py:327-328`.
34	- **In favour of raising:** a broken cookie setup would otherwise be invisible.
35	- **Against:** the webhook still grants the credits, so the person may pay again. The same raise fires on a history revisit after sign-out and on link scanners that re-fetch the address.
36	- **Confidence:** medium; this is a judgment call for Kenneth.
37	
38	**7. Account deletion now stops when Chargebee cannot find the subscription.** `jusprin/ledger/billing.py:164-171`.
39	- **When Chargebee says "not found":** the plan was bought on Obico's site before 2026-11-10 (commit `77fd19cadb` added the old handling), the subscription was deleted in Chargebee, the test site was cleared, or the plan row was made in the admin with an invented id.
40	- **What the person sees:** "Something went wrong on our side" on every attempt until one of us fixes the row by hand.
41	- **Verdict:** the owner is right under the rule, but nothing tells us the person is waiting on us.
42	- **Confidence:** high in code; production count unconfirmed.
43	
44	**8. JusPrin 1 webhook: raising for "no plan and no account" repeats monthly for deleted accounts.** `jusprin/jusprin_cb_views.py:127-141`.
45	- **Scenario:** a deleted Obico account's subscription keeps renewing. Each event is retried about seven times over two to three days, then Chargebee emails us.
46	- **Conflict with a recent decision:** commit `2168e238ce` (2026-11-21) chose to acknowledge exactly this for the prepaid pack.
47	- **False report:** a first purchase where the webhook beats the browser callback and the Chargebee email differs from the account's raises once, then heals on retry.
48	- **Confidence:** medium; unconfirmed that deleting an Obico account leaves the JusPrin 1 subscription live.
49	
50	**9. The same function looks up the account by email across all syndicates.** `jusprin/jusprin_cb_views.py:138`. This is older code the change moved, not new behaviour.
51	- **Scenario:** an address with both an Obico and a JusPrin 2 account raises `MultipleObjectsReturned`. If only the JusPrin 2 account remains, the JusPrin 1 plan lands on it, which then triggers finding 3.
52	- **Confidence:** high in code.
53	
54	**10. A turn that delivered only tool calls counts as "delivered".** `jusprin/v2/gateway.py:237-238`.
55	- **Scenario:** the follow-up fails on our side, the person sees no answer and stays charged.
56	- **Confidence:** high; this is stated in the docstring, so it is a policy question.
57	
58	**11. The refund runs after the failure answer is sent, and leaves no record.** `jusprin/v2/gateway.py:147-149`.
59	- **Scenario:** the Sentry report is captured before `credits_given_back` is set, and the charge row is deleted, so only the log line shows a refund happened.
60	- **Confidence:** high.
61	
62	**12. `test_the_same_turn_sent_again_after_a_failure_is_charged_again` passes on the old code.** `jusprin/v2/tests/test_gateway_failures.py:220`. One charge and 495 credits is the end state with or without a refund.
63	
64	**13. `test_a_truncated_photo_is_the_persons` passes only because its picture is 8×8.** `jusprin/v2/tests/test_print_reports.py:120`. I cut JPEGs of 64×64 and larger in half locally, and `verify()` accepted them. A real cut-off photo is stored and earns the reward.
65	
66	## What held up
67	
68	- **Refund mechanics:** a turn cannot be refunded twice, because the charge row is deleted under the person's row lock inside a transaction. Credits return to the lots that paid, and Billing and usage still adds up.
69	- **Unknown-plan webhook raise:** it is narrow, since only this server's own customer ids match, and Chargebee's retries redeliver once settings are fixed.
70	- **Photo errno split:** it held across 16,500 damaged files, on Pillow 11.1 locally; the server pins 13.0.
71	- **Outside services:** no test in the diff reaches one. Every Chargebee call is patched, and Sentry is unset in the container.
72	- **App behaviour:** each Retry sends a new turn id (`AgentHost.cpp:3360`).
73

I read the change against the rule and found one money hole, several failures sent to the wrong owner, and two weak tests. Both test suites pass. Everything below is traced in code unless marked; I ran no new tests.

All paths are under `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise/web_ent/`.

## Findings, most serious first

**1. A direct caller can get a delivered reply refunded.** `jusprin/v2/credits.py:70-80`, `jusprin/v2/gateway.py:148-149, 202`.
- **Scenario:** Someone calls the gateway with their own script, reads the whole reply, and drops the connection before the last event. The turn stays charged, but no "completed" mark is set. They then send the same turn id with `X-JusPrin-Chat-Title: %FF`, which raises `UnicodeDecodeError` after admission and costs no provider call. The top handler gives the turn's charge back.
- **Slower variant:** the "completed" mark lasts one hour (`TURN_TTL_SECONDS`), so replaying a turn id later with a failing request has the same effect.
- **Why:** the refund is keyed by turn id, not by whether the failing request made the charge. `admit` knows whether it charged in this call; refunding only then would close it.
- **Confidence:** high on the logic, not run.

**2. The app's own 120-second limit is treated as "the person stopped".** `jusprin/v2/gateway.py:239-243`.
- **Scenario:** The provider stalls or the reply runs long. The app cuts the request at 120 seconds (`ProviderProfile.hpp:64`, set as `CURLOPT_TIMEOUT`), while the server waits up to 300. The server sees a disconnect, keeps the charge and reports nothing. The person retries under a new turn id and pays again.
- **Why:** a failure on our side is recorded as the person's choice.
- **Confidence:** high on the code path; unconfirmed how often replies pass 120 seconds.

**3. Billing and usage now fails for a paid account with no customer on JusPrin 2's Chargebee site.** `jusprin/ledger/billing.py:152-156`, `jusprin/ledger/ledger.py:35-44`.
- **Scenario:** `has_paid` is true for a JusPrin 1 plan row, a plan row made in the admin, or a plan bought before the 2026-11-10 move to JusPrin's own site. Chargebee answers "not found" for these, every time, so the page is a 500 for that person on every visit.
- **Why:** the new docstring says such an account always has a customer; `ensure_customer` in the same file treats a missing customer as normal.
- **Gap in the test:** the new test covers only a 401.
- **Confidence:** high in code; unconfirmed whether production has such accounts.

**4. Starting a checkout without a signed-in browser is sent to us, but it is a stale page.** `jusprin/v2/web.py:305-306`.
- **How it is reached:** the post needs a valid CSRF cookie and token, so strangers and crawlers get Django's 403 and never reach it. What does reach it is a tab left open past the 60-day session, a guest link (`?guest=1` logs out without changing the CSRF cookie) opened later in the same browser, or an account deleted while the page is open.
- **Why:** all of these are the person's, and the report names no account, so we cannot act on it. `billing_page`, `cancel` and `portal` in the same file treat the same cause as the person's.
- **Confidence:** high.

**5. Opening the checkout return address without an id files a report.** `jusprin/v2/web.py:325-326`.
- **Scenario:** the address is a public GET with no sign-in check before the raise. Any scanner or person who requests it gets a 500 and files "Chargebee sent the person back…", though nothing ties the request to Chargebee.
- **Confidence:** high on reachability; volume unconfirmed.

**6. Coming back from paying without the session shows "Something went wrong on our side" to someone whose payment succeeded.** `jusprin/v2/web.py:327-328`.
- **In favour of raising:** a broken cookie setup would otherwise be invisible.
- **Against:** the webhook still grants the credits, so the person may pay again. The same raise fires on a history revisit after sign-out and on link scanners that re-fetch the address.
- **Confidence:** medium; this is a judgment call for Kenneth.

**7. Account deletion now stops when Chargebee cannot find the subscription.** `jusprin/ledger/billing.py:164-171`.
- **When Chargebee says "not found":** the plan was bought on Obico's site before 2026-11-10 (commit `77fd19cadb` added the old handling), the subscription was deleted in Chargebee, the test site was cleared, or the plan row was made in the admin with an invented id.
- **What the person sees:** "Something went wrong on our side" on every attempt until one of us fixes the row by hand.
- **Verdict:** the owner is right under the rule, but nothing tells us the person is waiting on us.
- **Confidence:** high in code; production count unconfirmed.

**8. JusPrin 1 webhook: raising for "no plan and no account" repeats monthly for deleted accounts.** `jusprin/jusprin_cb_views.py:127-141`.
- **Scenario:** a deleted Obico account's subscription keeps renewing. Each event is retried about seven times over two to three days, then Chargebee emails us.
- **Conflict with a recent decision:** commit `2168e238ce` (2026-11-21) chose to acknowledge exactly this for the prepaid pack.
- **False report:** a first purchase where the webhook beats the browser callback and the Chargebee email differs from the account's raises once, then heals on retry.
- **Confidence:** medium; unconfirmed that deleting an Obico account leaves the JusPrin 1 subscription live.

**9. The same function looks up the account by email across all syndicates.** `jusprin/jusprin_cb_views.py:138`. This is older code the change moved, not new behaviour.
- **Scenario:** an address with both an Obico and a JusPrin 2 account raises `MultipleObjectsReturned`. If only the JusPrin 2 account remains, the JusPrin 1 plan lands on it, which then triggers finding 3.
- **Confidence:** high in code.

**10. A turn that delivered only tool calls counts as "delivered".** `jusprin/v2/gateway.py:237-238`.
- **Scenario:** the follow-up fails on our side, the person sees no answer and stays charged.
- **Confidence:** high; this is stated in the docstring, so it is a policy question.

**11. The refund runs after the failure answer is sent, and leaves no record.** `jusprin/v2/gateway.py:147-149`.
- **Scenario:** the Sentry report is captured before `credits_given_back` is set, and the charge row is deleted, so only the log line shows a refund happened.
- **Confidence:** high.

**12. `test_the_same_turn_sent_again_after_a_failure_is_charged_again` passes on the old code.** `jusprin/v2/tests/test_gateway_failures.py:220`. One charge and 495 credits is the end state with or without a refund.

**13. `test_a_truncated_photo_is_the_persons` passes only because its picture is 8×8.** `jusprin/v2/tests/test_print_reports.py:120`. I cut JPEGs of 64×64 and larger in half locally, and `verify()` accepted them. A real cut-off photo is stored and earns the reward.

## What held up

- **Refund mechanics:** a turn cannot be refunded twice, because the charge row is deleted under the person's row lock inside a transaction. Credits return to the lots that paid, and Billing and usage still adds up.
- **Unknown-plan webhook raise:** it is narrow, since only this server's own customer ids match, and Chargebee's retries redeliver once settings are fixed.
- **Photo errno split:** it held across 16,500 damaged files, on Pillow 11.1 locally; the server pins 13.0.
- **Outside services:** no test in the diff reaches one. Every Chargebee call is patched, and Sentry is unset in the container.
- **App behaviour:** each Retry sends a new turn id (`AgentHost.cpp:3360`).

## Test results

- `jusprin.v2.tests`: 348 tests, OK.
- `app_ent`: 56 tests, OK.

## What I read

- **Fully:** the diff, the Error handling section of `CLAUDE.md`, `v2/web.py`, `v2/views.py`, `v2/gateway.py`, `v2/credits.py`, `ledger/ledger.py`, `ledger/billing.py`, `ledger/reports.py`, `ledger/models.py`, `jusprin_cb_views.py`, `test_account_delete.py`, `prices.html`.
- **In part:** the other test files, `app_ent/cb_views.py`, `ledger/account.py`, the middleware, the settings, the app's `ServerSheet` and `ProviderAgent`.
- **Not read:** `upstream.py`, `stream.py`, `capture.py`, `errors.py`, the allauth sign-in code.

Sources:
- [Chargebee Events API](https://apidocs.chargebee.com/docs/api/events.md)
- [Chargebee: webhook failure email](https://support.chargebee.com/support/solutions/articles/247817-i-received-a-webhook-failure-email-from-chargebee-how-to-fix-this-)
- [Chargebee: how to know a webhook is failing](https://support.chargebee.com/support/solutions/articles/215220-how-would-i-know-if-the-configured-webhook-url-in-my-chargebee-site-is-failing-)

            'it cannot stream from a Django view in this Django version')

        # this one every sync_to_async call below would run on asgiref's single
        # thread per process, behind every websocket consumer's database work.
        # Django's own ASGI handler opens one per request in the same way.
        async with ThreadSensitiveContext():
            # Django's own handler brackets every request with these signals;
            # they are what closes stale database connections.
            await sync_to_async(signals.request_started.send, thread_sensitive=True)(
                sender=self.__class__, scope=scope)

                await self._handle(scope, receive, send)
            finally:
                await sync_to_async(_finish_request, thread_sensitive=True)(self.__class__)

        """The endpoint's one top handler. A failure nothing expected reaches
        here unchanged: it is reported, and the app is told only that something
        went wrong on our side, as an answer before the reply starts or as the
        stream's last event after. The report carries everything known about
        the request by the time it failed."""

        # decided it recorded it in the facts: the log keeps it as well as the

                raise GatewayError(400, 'invalid_request', 'The X-JusPrin-Chat header must be 32 lowercase hex digits.')

            raw_body = await _read_body(receive, settings.JUSPRIN_V2_MAX_BODY_BYTES)

                # to stall every websocket this process serves.

            else:

"""SSE passthrough with the upstream hidden.

Events are forwarded as they arrive. Only events that name the upstream model
are rewritten; every other event keeps its fields as upstream sent them (line
endings are normalised to \\n). An event that says the reply failed is never
forwarded: EventRewriter.failure names it, and the gateway answers instead.
"""
import json
from typing import AsyncIterator, Dict, List, Optional

# The events that end a reply that did not fail.
FINAL_EVENTS = {'anthropic': {'message_stop'}, 'responses': {'response.completed', 'response.incomplete'}}


class EventRewriter:
    """Rewrites one stream's events for the client and collects token usage."""

    def __init__(self, fmt: str, alias_id: str):
        self.fmt = fmt
        self.alias_id = alias_id
        self.usage: Dict[str, int] = {}
        self.finished = False  # the reply's final event has gone through
        self.last_event = None  # the type of the last event rewritten

    def failure(self, lines: List[str]) -> Optional[dict]:
        """The event, as the provider sent it, when it says the reply failed;
        None otherwise."""
        data = _data(lines)
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            return None
        kind = data.get('type')
        if kind == 'error' or (self.fmt == 'responses' and kind == 'response.failed'):
            return data
        return None

    def rewrite(self, lines: List[str]) -> bytes:
        data = _data(lines)
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            self.last_event = data.get('type')
            self.finished = self.finished or self.last_event in FINAL_EVENTS[self.fmt]
            if self._rewrite(data):
                kept = [line for line in lines if not line.startswith('data:')]
                lines = kept + ['data: ' + json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':'))]
        return ('\n'.join(lines) + '\n\n').encode()

    def _rewrite(self, data: dict) -> bool:
        """Edits data in place; True when anything changed."""
        if self.fmt == 'anthropic':
            return self._rewrite_anthropic(data)
        return self._rewrite_responses(data)

    def _rewrite_anthropic(self, data: dict) -> bool:
        kind = data.get('type')
        if kind == 'message_start' and isinstance(data.get('message'), dict):
            message = data['message']
            self._add_usage(message.get('usage'))
            if 'model' in message:
                message['model'] = self.alias_id
                return True
        elif kind == 'message_delta':
            self._add_usage(data.get('usage'))
        return False

    def _rewrite_responses(self, data: dict) -> bool:
        kind = data.get('type')
        changed = False
        response = data.get('response')
        if isinstance(response, dict):
            # Every response.* lifecycle event (created, in_progress, completed,
            # incomplete, failed) carries the whole response object, model included.
            if 'model' in response:
                response['model'] = self.alias_id
                changed = True
            if kind == 'response.completed':
                self._add_usage(response.get('usage'))
        return changed

    def _add_usage(self, usage):
        if not isinstance(usage, dict):
            return
        for key, value in usage.items():
            if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool):
                # Anthropic repeats running totals in message_delta; the last
                # value is the turn's figure, so assignment is right for both.
                self.usage[key] = value
            elif isinstance(value, dict):  # Responses' *_tokens_details
                for sub_key, sub_value in value.items():
                    if isinstance(sub_value, int) and not isinstance(sub_value, bool):
                        self.usage[f'{key}.{sub_key}'] = sub_value


def _data(lines: List[str]):
    """An event's data, parsed; None when it has none or it is not JSON."""
    data_lines = [line[5:].removeprefix(' ') for line in lines if line.startswith('data:')]
    if not data_lines:
        return None
    try:
        return json.loads('\n'.join(data_lines))
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return None


def gateway_error_event(fmt: str, code: str, message: str) -> bytes:
    """An in-stream error the gateway itself raises after the 200 has gone out,
    in the shape the endpoint's format uses for its own error events."""
    if fmt == 'anthropic':
        data = {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'api_error', 'code': code, 'message': message}}
    else:
        data = {'type': 'error', 'code': code, 'message': message}
    return f'event: error\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n'.encode()


async def sse_events(lines: AsyncIterator[str]) -> AsyncIterator[List[str]]:
    """Groups SSE lines into events. An event left unterminated when the stream
    ends is dropped, as the SSE spec requires."""
    event: List[str] = []
    async for line in lines:
        if line:
            event.append(line)
        elif event:
            yield event
            event = []
"""Per-turn admission: rate limit, then the turn's charge in the credit ledger.

A turn is everything the client sends for one reply, including tool-call
follow-ups; every request of it carries the same X-JusPrin-Turn value. A turn
pays its model's price once, however many requests it makes. Title requests are
free, and a request of kind "note" is a turn the app started, not the person.

The reply requests of one turn are sequential (a follow-up is built from the
previous answer), so the charge does not guard against two reply requests of
the same turn racing each other.
"""
import enum
import time

from django.conf import settings

from jusprin.ledger.ledger import charge_turn, give_back_turn
from jusprin.ledger.models import CreditCharge
from lib.cache import REDIS

KEY_PREFIX = 'jusprin:v2'
TURN_TTL_SECONDS = 60 * 60


class Admission(enum.Enum):
    ADMITTED = 'admitted'
    RATE_LIMITED = 'rate_limited'


def admit(user_id: int, turn_id: str, request_kind: str, alias, chat_id: str = None) -> Admission:
    """Count a new turn against the rate limit, then charge it once unless it
    is a title. Raises ledger.CreditsExhausted when it cannot be paid.
    Synchronous: Redis and the credit tables are both blocking."""
    seen_key = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:seen:{user_id}:{turn_id}'
    if REDIS.set(seen_key, '1', nx=True, ex=TURN_TTL_SECONDS):
        bucket = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:turns:{user_id}:{int(time.time() // 60)}'
        pipe = REDIS.pipeline()
        pipe.incr(bucket)
        pipe.expire(bucket, 120)
        turns_this_minute, _ = pipe.execute()
        if turns_this_minute > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_TURNS_PER_MINUTE:
            # The turn was not admitted, so its retry is a new turn again.
            REDIS.delete(seen_key)
            return Admission.RATE_LIMITED

    if request_kind == 'title':
        return Admission.ADMITTED

    charged_key = f'{KEY_PREFIX}:charged:{user_id}:{turn_id}'
    if not REDIS.set(charged_key, '1', nx=True, ex=TURN_TTL_SECONDS):
        return Admission.ADMITTED
    origin = CreditCharge.APP if request_kind == 'note' else CreditCharge.PERSON
    charged = False
    try:
        charge_turn(user_id, turn_id, alias, origin, chat_id)
        charged = True
    finally:
        # Only a turn that actually paid is remembered as paid, whether the
        # credits ran out or the credit tables raised.
        if not charged:
            REDIS.delete(charged_key)
    return Admission.ADMITTED
